[measurement]{.chip .measured} Entry 56 · milestone M4
:::

The richer local diagnostic saved its complete collection before offline tracking
failed. Repeated input filenames collided in a tracker that copies by basename.
The original scheduler failure stays recorded. An archive with relative case paths
now retains the original files, their provenance and checksum; recovery required
no additional solver calls.

| evidence | conclusion |
|---|---|
| direct signed collection and saved-output audit | [648 integrity checks pass on the complete 15-state collection; all affected signed states agree between backends, but four control states fail the existing parity criterion; original terminal tracking failure is preserved and archive recovery calls no solver]{.claim}[C-199](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-199){.cid .st-measured} |
| repeatability tooling | [31 synthetic diagnostic tests pass in each mode, including archive identity and repeatability completeness/discrepancy checks; 33 unchanged focused records are retained, giving 64 focused recorded passes per mode]{.claim}[C-200](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-200){.cid .st-tested} |
| coupled reference acceptance | unresolved; the original uncovered face remains |

The collection confirms signed energy flux where the previous coefficient inversion
had only inferred it. It also reveals backend discrepancies in preceding controls.
Agreement at the affected states does not excuse disagreement elsewhere, and a
successful spectral integration is not an independent physics validation.

The owner delegated a literature-based review of what the reference should be.
Primary TGLF documentation defines species energy fluxes and separate mode outputs.
Published validation studies compare matched inputs, spectra, fluxes and coupled
profiles. Literature also contains mechanisms for inward energy transport, but
their existence does not identify the mechanism in these particular inputs.

The approved method preserves signed, separate-species TGLF transport as the target
reference and requires numerical reproducibility before a coupled comparison.
The current guarded trajectory remains a regression baseline. Clipping the signed
output would define a different modelling baseline; it cannot retroactively supply
missing reference coverage. A conservative stable energy closure needs its own
concrete implementation review. The served surrogate contract and current guard
stay unchanged. M4 and its temperature gate remain open.

**What's next.** Run a frozen bounded repeatability check, keeping each fresh
backend evaluation and every discrepancy. Then review numerical convergence and
the energy closure. No remote artifact
synchronization has occurred.
